what: Mind-only accepted as the conventional truth and as a stage of meditation before the imageless (Śāntarakṣita, Kamalaśīla).

evidence.detail: Kamalaśīla quotes Laṅkāvatāra 10.256–258 in Bhāvanākrama I and the Madhyamakāloka
Tibetan doxography names the school 'Yogācāra-Svātantrika-Madhyamaka'

what: The whole Indian Yogācāra system as compiled in the Cheng weishi lun.

evidence.detail: Xuanzang's studies at Nālandā under Śīlabhadra and translation of the Yogācārabhūmi
Cheng weishi lun commenting the Triṃśikā

what: The Laṅkāvatāra's mind-only teaching transmitted by the early 'Laṅkā masters'; the language of the ālaya and of the mind's original purity.

evidence.detail: Bodhidharma is said to have given Huike the four-fascicle Laṅkāvatāra
mind-only, the storehouse, turning the basis

what: The three natures and the Maitreya texts read as teaching an ultimate empty of what is other (shentong).

evidence.detail: Dolpopa's Mountain Doctrine cites the Maitreya texts and three-nature passages
the Jonang count the Maitreya texts as definitive third-turning teachings

what: The dream argument against external objects, the language of consciousness 'vibrating' as duality, and non-origination in Māṇḍūkya Kārikā ch. 4.

evidence.detail: Māṇḍūkya Kārikā 4 argues from dream against external objects and uses Yogācāra-like terms (e.g. vijñāna-spandita)
direction and extent of influence debated; the Advaita tradition denies dependence (see dsp:advaita-crypto-buddhism)

notes: Advaita tradition's own view: Gauḍapāda expounds the Upaniṣads; resemblance to Buddhist terms is polemical adaptation. Recorded as disputed.

what: The two-means framework reinterpreted (pratyakṣa/parokṣa), the debate over the triple-marked reason (answered by 'anyathānupapatti' as the sole mark), and the genres of logic manuals.

evidence.detail: Pātrasvāmin's verse 'anyathānupapannatvaṃ yatra tatra trayeṇa kim' is quoted in the Tattvasaṃgraha (recalled)
Akalaṅka, Haribhadra and Prabhācandra comment on or refute Dharmakīrti; Haribhadra comments on the Nyāyapraveśa (local e-text)

what: Verses of the Vākyapadīya reworked in Dignāga's Trikālaparīkṣā; themes of word and meaning that shape the apoha theory.

evidence.detail: Trikālaparīkṣā (D4207) parallels Vākyapadīya verses (scholarly finding)
the influence on apoha is a scholarly reconstruction

what: Momentariness, causal efficacy as the criterion of reality, and the image-bearing (sākāra) cognition inferred to have an external cause.

evidence.detail: Tibetan doxography classifies the pramāṇa school as 'Sautrāntika following reasoning' at one level
santāna, kṣaṇika, arthakriyā

what: The epistemological curriculum (Pramāṇavārttika, Pramāṇaviniścaya), the Collected Topics debate method and the tenet-system classification.

evidence.detail: Ngok Loden Sherab and Chapa at Sangphu; Sakya Paṇḍita's Treasury of Reasoning; Gelug monastic debate
Gyaltsab's commentary on the Pramāṇavārttika

what: Utpaladeva states the Buddhist logicians' position (momentary cognitions, no enduring knower, apoha, self-awareness) as the pūrvapakṣa of the Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā and turns its tools (ābhāsa, self-awareness, the refutation of external objects) toward a single conscious Lord.

evidence.detail: ĪPK 1.2 sets out the Buddhist objections (recalled)
svasaṃvedana, ābhāsa, vikalpa, apoha
